content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm experiencing issues with a [product_name] communication module. Initially, an older SIM card from the carrier was working fine, but after being unused for a while, the phone number was deactivated. We tried new SIM cards from the same provider, but none were recognized by the module. Switching to another carrier worked briefly in my office—confirmed by the module connecting to the network on the status screen. However, when tested elsewhere, I received a diagnostic message indicating the module couldn't connect to the mobile wireless network. Upon checking, I found it had automatically connected to the previous carrier instead of the intended one. Testing the SIM card in a mobile phone confirmed it works, and restarting the module did not help. Is there a way to manually select which network it connects to? Regards.
Hello [user_name], If your provider's mobile network becomes unreachable and you have enabled the "Allow roaming" option, the module will connect to any available mobile network.

Hi [user_name], I've tried enabling and disabling roaming, but it hasn't helped—the device still connects to the wrong network and won't allow mobile data. Should I restart the module after making changes?
Hello, Please try restarting the module as suggested. If it still doesn't resolve the issue, consider performing a factory reset and reconfiguring everything from the beginning.

Still no solution. The device continues to connect to a network but won't allow for a mobile connection. I also updated the firmware and performed a factory reset before reconfiguring, but no luck. Should I reach out to the carrier?

Try these steps first, if you haven't done so yet: 1. Remove the SIM card. 2. In the web management tool, go to the 'WAN' > 'Mobile wireless settings' tab and uncheck the 'Activate mobile wireless interface' option to turn it off. 3. Power down the module by holding the SET button for 5 to 10 seconds until all LEDs are off. 4. Disconnect the module from its power supply. 5. Remove and then reinsert the SIM card. 6. Restore power to the module. 7. Go back to the same settings tab and check 'Activate mobile wireless interface'. 8. Enter the SIM card's PIN in the settings. If this doesn't help, it's recommended to contact support.
At the moment, it's working in the original location where I tested it, but I'll try the suggested solution again in an area with connectivity problems. Thanks for your support—I'll keep you posted.

Hi [user_name], Could you share what steps you took to get it working? Any specific action that made the difference? I'm facing a similar issue and would appreciate any advice or details about what you did differently. Thank you.

Hello, I haven't been able to resolve the issue completely. Occasionally, SMS messages are received even when it's connected to the wrong network, but sending them is unreliable. Try repositioning the antenna, as signal location seems to be a major factor. In some areas, the correct network connects, but in others, it doesn't. Best of luck.

Hi [user_name], Thanks for your response. I was able to resolve the connectivity problem—previous attempts may have failed due to missing steps. Make sure that the 'Enable mobile wireless interface' box is unchecked when swapping SIM cards. With the module powered off, insert the new SIM card, power it up, and check the 'Enable mobile wireless interface' option followed by 'Apply'. Confirm 'Mobile Wireless Interface Connection Established: Yes' is shown, then you can send and receive SMS. To change SIM cards again, uncheck 'Enable mobile wireless interface', hit 'Apply', go to maintenance and set the module to safe status, power off, swap SIMs, power back on, login, and enable the mobile wireless interface followed by 'Apply'. Once 'Connection Established: Yes' is shown, SMS functionality should work.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report that the [product_name] module automatically connects to unintended mobile networks after SIM card changes or relocation, leading to unreliable connections. Manual network selection is unavailable, and troubleshooting with firmware updates, resets, and configuration does not always work. Signal location heavily impacts connectivity, adding further unpredictability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to manually select or prioritize mobile networks on the [product_name] module for consistent connectivity and reliable SMS operations, regardless of location. They also expect clear and repeatable troubleshooting steps to restore connections as needed.
